mood.summary: Fear is still running high. On Nov 5 the S&P 500 fell 4.4% and the Nasdaq slid into a correction, the worst day since April 2025, on worries that election results will slow AI and data-centre spending. The Fear & Greed index sits in Extreme Fear at 20, and bearish individual investors outnumber bulls by about 14 points. Stocks are bouncing on Nov 6 after a strong jobs report (165,000 jobs vs about 60,000 expected), but that also firmed bets on a December Fed rate hike.

trending.note: Board as of Saturday 4:07 PM ET; prices are the Nov 13 close. Why-it's-trending notes summarize the Stocktwits stream and the news it links to.

items.name: L3Harris Technologies
items.about: L3Harris is a US defense and aerospace contractor that also builds and maintains FAA air traffic communications systems.
items.why: Chatter spiked Saturday after Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said officials are investigating whether L3Harris was responsible for the FAA air traffic control failure that halted US flights nationwide for more than four hours on Friday (reported by Bloomberg and Investing.com). The stock closed Friday up 0.19% at $272.35, before the probe news; posts say Monday's open is the test.

items.name: Alpha Tau Medical
items.about: Alpha Tau is an Israeli medtech company developing Alpha DaRT, implantable seeds that deliver alpha radiation directly into solid tumors.
items.why: Alpha Tau presented updated REGAIN trial data in recurrent glioblastoma at the SNO meeting after Friday's close; posts cite a 100% response rate and 83.3% complete responses among 6 evaluable patients, with all 8 treated patients alive. That builds on May interim data showing 2 complete responses in the first 3 patients. An investor call is set for Monday 8:30 AM ET.

items.name: BitMine Immersion Technologies
items.about: BitMine holds a large Ethereum treasury and runs bitcoin mining operations, so its shares trade closely with ether.
items.why: Shares fell 4.7% Friday as crypto kept sliding, and posts flag a weak Monday after ether dropped about 5% more on Saturday to near $1,840. The stock tracks the ETH price closely, so the weekend crypto slide is the main driver of the chatter.

items.name: Grayscale Ethereum Mini Trust
items.about: A Grayscale exchange-traded trust that holds ether, giving brokerage accounts exposure to the Ethereum price.
items.why: The trust fell 3.3% Friday as ether extended a multi-day slide, and posts show ether down roughly another 5% Saturday to about $1,840. Bitcoin's break below $72,000 earlier in the week, with over $650 million of leveraged positions liquidated, set the risk-off tone.

items.name: Transocean
items.about: Transocean is an offshore drilling contractor that leases deepwater and harsh-environment rigs to oil producers.
items.why: Shares rose 4.1% Friday to $5.54 on heavy volume of 30 million shares as offshore drillers caught a bid. Posts tie it to more tanker strikes and retaliation in the Gulf lifting oil-risk worries, and to SLB being picked to run drilling services on two Transocean rigs for Vår Energi in Norway for up to eight years.

items.name: Bitwise XRP ETF
items.about: A Bitwise exchange-traded fund that holds XRP, the token tied to Ripple's payments network.
items.why: The ETF slipped 1% Friday, but chatter rose over the weekend as XRP fell about 6.6% Saturday to below $1, according to posted price updates. The move is part of a broad crypto drawdown that also hit bitcoin, ether and solana.

items.name: Direxion Daily GOOGL Bull 2X
items.about: A leveraged ETF that aims to return twice Alphabet's daily stock move.
items.why: Alphabet briefly topped $300 midweek as it led hyperscalers while Nvidia stumbled on leadership turmoil, and posts frame Nvidia's pain as Google's gain in the AI trade. GGLL gave back 2.1% Friday after opening near $74, in line with a softer tech tape.

items.name: Delta Air Lines
items.about: Delta is one of the largest US airlines, with hubs in Atlanta, Detroit, Minneapolis and New York.
items.why: Friday's nationwide air traffic control outage grounded US flights for more than four hours, and the FAA warned 4,000 to 5,000 more flights could be cancelled Saturday as airlines recover. Shares slipped 0.35% Friday; posts note Delta had guided to only a 7-9% Q4 operating margin and had $6.9 billion of liquidity at Sep 30.

items.name: Vertex Pharmaceuticals
items.about: Vertex is a biotech company best known for its cystic fibrosis medicines, now expanding into kidney disease, pain and other areas.
items.why: The FDA decision on povetacicept for IgA nephropathy is due by November 30 under the accelerated approval path. Posts cite RAINIER trial data showing a 52% cut in proteinuria at week 36 versus 4.3% on placebo; the stock eased 0.7% Friday to $538.60 after earlier this month reporting 12% revenue growth and raising guidance.

items.name: Renaissance IPO ETF
items.about: An ETF that holds recently listed US companies, giving a basket exposure to the new-issue market.
items.why: Interest is building around Anthropic's planned Nasdaq listing under ANT, which Renaissance Capital expects to price during the week of November 16; the amended filing sets a $70 to $78 range for 825 million shares. The ETF fell 1.3% Friday and slipped further after hours as other deals priced below range or were postponed.

items.name: Teva Pharmaceutical
items.about: Teva is a global drugmaker selling generics plus branded drugs such as the migraine treatment AJOVY and Austedo.
items.why: Shares rose 1.9% Friday to $44.50 as the stock kept climbing. On Saturday, partner NeuroGen announced that AJOVY was added to China's national reimbursement drug list after price negotiations. Posts also watch for pipeline updates on Igalmi and ecopipam.

items.name: Health Care Select Sector SPDR
items.about: An ETF holding the large-cap US healthcare stocks in the S&P 500, from drugmakers to insurers and device makers.
items.why: The fund rose 0.5% Friday to $188.85 as healthcare kept attracting money while tech and crypto sold off. Posts note the sector has become a crowded trade well above support after a rebound from September lows.

items.name: Summit Therapeutics
items.about: Summit is a biotech developing ivonescimab, a PD-1/VEGF bispecific antibody for lung cancer, licensed from China's Akeso.
items.why: The FDA's goal date for ivonescimab plus chemo in EGFR-mutated lung cancer after TKI therapy is November 14, and no decision had been reported as of Saturday afternoon. The filing rests on the HARMONi trial, which missed its overall survival endpoint, so Fierce Pharma calls the outcome uncertain. Shares fell 6.2% Friday; posts cite roughly 28% short interest in the float.

items.name: Grayscale Bitcoin Mini Trust
items.about: A Grayscale exchange-traded trust that holds bitcoin, giving brokerage accounts exposure to the BTC price.
items.why: The trust fell 3.5% Friday and bitcoin kept dropping Saturday to about $65,800, down about 4% on the day per posted price updates. Earlier this week bitcoin lost its 50-week average below $72,000 as more than $650 million of leveraged bets were liquidated; posts say some money is rotating toward the Anthropic IPO.

items.name: WhiteFiber
items.about: WhiteFiber runs AI data centers and GPU cloud services for model-training customers.
items.why: Shares fell 8.8% Friday to $9.43 as AI data-center stocks sold off alongside crypto miners. Posts cite an $865 million 10-year contracted backlog at its North Carolina campus and an H.C. Wainwright target raised to $36, while bears call the group overvalued.

items.name: Trulieve Cannabis
items.about: Trulieve is one of the largest US multi-state cannabis operators, with a big footprint in Florida.
items.why: Trulieve appeared on the preliminary list of additions to the Russell 3000 index, which would bring index-fund buying. Traders are also waiting on the DEA rescheduling process after a judge's review. Shares fell 2.2% Friday to $10.90.

items.name: Novo Nordisk
items.about: Novo Nordisk is a Danish drugmaker behind the diabetes and obesity drugs Ozempic and Wegovy.
items.why: Shares rose 2.4% Friday to $41.63, a fourth straight weekly gain. Posts contrast Lilly's oral obesity pill in a Japanese trial (7.9% weight loss) with Novo's own data and recirculate September's CagriSema result of about 21% weight loss. An FDA decision on CagriSema is expected in Q4.

items.name: GraniteShares 2x Long NVDA
items.about: A leveraged ETF that aims to return twice Nvidia's daily stock move.
items.why: Nvidia is under a board investigation into CEO Jensen Huang, and the Wall Street Journal reported the board may oust him, which pushed shares down 21% from their October peak. NVDL fell 4% Friday. Nvidia reports earnings on November 17 against $108 billion revenue guidance, and posts flag large bullish call buying.

items.name: Starbucks
items.about: Starbucks is the world's largest coffeehouse chain.
items.why: The stock is trading just under $110 after beating estimates on Oct 29 ($0.80 adjusted EPS vs about $0.71 expected), and unusual call buying of 30,000-plus contracts was flagged earlier in the week. It slipped 0.2% Friday; posts debate whether high menu prices will hurt traffic.

items.name: LightPath Technologies
items.about: LightPath makes optical components and infrared imaging systems for defense, industrial and telecom customers.
items.why: LightPath reported fiscal Q1 revenue of $20.8 million and a record $132.9 million backlog on November 10, but shares fell 5.1% Friday to $6.84. Posts say the stock is down about 50% in three months and point to possible tax-loss selling.
